name: Temur Battlecrier
oracle_text: During your turn, spells you cast cost {1} less to cast for each creature you control with power 4 or greater.
blocked_sentences: During your turn, spells you cast cost {1} less to cast for each creature you control with power 4 or greater.

needs.what: a `power` (and, for its twin, `toughness`) key admitted into the filter language a STATIC ability may read -- STATIC_FILTER_KEYS / STATIC_COUNT_FILTER_KEYS in src/automtg/cards/loader/vocabulary.py, matched by `characteristics._matches` / `_count_matching` -- so that a static's magnitude can be `{"count": {"controller": "you", "types": ["Creature"], "power": {">=": 4}}}`. The whole rest of this card is already sayable: a `spell_cost_reduction` static with `affects_spells: {"controller": "you"}`, `condition: {"is_your_turn": true}` (`_battlefield_statics` gates every static on `_static_active`, so the "During your turn" clause is honoured) and `amount` evaluated by `_static_value`, which already dispatches `count` to `_count_matching`. Only the filter key is missing. The hard part is deliberate and is where the work is: power is a DERIVED characteristic, computed by the layered `chars` pipeline, while every key in STATIC_FILTER_KEYS today is a pipeline INPUT (printed types, colours, mana cost, controller, tap state), precisely so that a static's own magnitude cannot depend on another static's output. Admitting power needs a defined answer to the cycle -- e.g. reading power at a fixed, earlier layer (printed P/T plus counters, before other statics' buffs), or a documented dependency order in the pipeline -- and the answer has to hold for the cost-reduction readers too, which run at legality and payment time outside `chars`. This single key unblocks the whole ferocious family of statics ("as long as you control a creature with power 4 or greater", "for each creature you control with power 4 or greater"), which today can only be written on the effect side.
needs.why_existing_wont_do: The near miss is `count`, and it is blocked at the loader, not at the reader: `spell_cost_reduction`'s `amount` goes through `_validate_static_value` -> `_validate_static_count_filter`, whose battlefield branch allows only STATIC_COUNT_FILTER_KEYS = STATIC_FILTER_KEYS | {zone, name}, and that set has no `power` -- the comment on the set says why (a static may only read printed characteristics). `power` IS in `selector_keys`, but that is the effect-side selector language, which a static may not use; writing it here is a DslError, not a silent miscount. The same wall stands in front of every other spelling. `exists` in `static_condition_keys` is validated by the same `_validate_static_count_filter`, so even the weaker "as long as you control a creature with power 4 or greater" cannot be asked. The card-level `cost_reduction` field is the wrong direction entirely -- `costs.cost_reduction`'s docstring says it discounts the card that CARRIES it (Ghalta), not the other spells this creature is discounting -- and its filter is held to STATIC_FILTER_KEYS | COST_REDUCTION_FILTER_KEYS, neither of which has `power` either. `total_power` is in COST_REDUCTION_KEYS and is a different number: it sums the power of everything matching the filter, so two 4/4s and a 1/1 would discount {9} where the card says {2}, and it is not reachable from a `spell_cost_reduction` static anyway, whose `amount` is static-value language rather than reduction language. Nothing in `static_value_keys` measures power: `count` counts objects, `mana_symbols` reads printed costs, `counters_on` reads counters, and `max_count_of`/`min_count_of` are per-player counts of the same power-blind filter. An approximation by proxy -- counting creatures by mana value, by subtype, or dropping the power clause and discounting for each creature -- is a materially different card in the sandbox's own position (two creatures of unasserted printed power), which is exactly the case where a wrong encoding passes a gate and ships.

notes: One sentence, one blocker, so no partial answer was written -- dropping or weakening the power clause would leave the card's only printed line implemented as a different discount, and there is no second line for an ability to claim. Once the key exists this card has a real gate-5 assertion available beyond `{"zone": "battlefield"}`: it is a 4/3, so the Battlecrier itself satisfies its own filter, and `battlefield_count` 33 holds.
